ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is an AC series circuit. The two terminals on the left side are the power supply terminals; V1 is connected between the upper and lower ends on the left side, measuring the total voltage of the whole circuit. In the upper branch there is a capacitor C; the two ends of V2 are connected respectively to the left and right sides of capacitor C, so V2 measures the capacitor voltage |V_C|. The node on the right side of the capacitor is connected downward to a resistor R and an inductor L in series; V3 on the right side is connected across the two ends of this R-L series branch, so V3 measures |V_RL|. Reasoning: The problem gives that all voltmeter readings are 220 V, and R = 10 Ω, so |V1| = |V2| = |V3|. This circuit is equivalent to capacitor C in series with the R-L series branch, so the same current I flows through each component. Dividing the three equal voltage amplitudes by the same current I gives equal reactance/impedance magnitudes: X_C = |Z_RL| = |Z_total|. Among them |Z_RL| = sqrt(R^2 + X_L^2), while the total impedance magnitude |Z_total| = sqrt(R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2). Therefore X_C^2 = R^2 + X_L^2, and X_C^2 = R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2. Subtracting the two equations gives X_L^2 = (X_L - X_C)^2. Taking the physical nonzero solution gives X_C = 2X_L. Substituting into X_C^2 = R^2 + X_L^2: 4X_L^2 = R^2 + X_L^2, so 3X_L^2 = R^2. Thus X_L = R/sqrt(3) = 10/sqrt(3) ≈ 5.77 Ω, approximately 5.8 Ω.

method.method_draft: From the image identify V2 as measuring |V_C|, V3 as measuring |V_RL|, and V1 as measuring |V_total|. Thus X_L = R/sqrt(3) = 10/sqrt(3) ≈ 5.77 Ω, approximately 5.8 Ω.
